title: Plasticity of Expression of Stem Cell and EMT Markers in Breast Cancer Cells in 2D and 3D Culture Depend on the Spatial Parameters of Cell Growth; Mathematical Modeling of Mechanical Stress in Cell Culture in Relation to ECM Stiffness
content: The majority of the current cancer research is based on two-dimensional cell cultures and animal models. These methods have limitations, including different expression of key factors involved in carcinogenesis and metastasis, depending on culture conditions. Addressing these differences is crucial in obtaining physiologically relevant models. In this manuscript we analyzed the plasticity of expression of stem cell and epithelial/mesenchymal markers in breast cancer cells, depending on culture conditions. Significant differences in markers expression in different growth conditions were observed, not only between 2D and 3D conditions, but also between two different 3D models. Differences observed in the levels of adherent junction protein E-cadherin in a two different 3D models suggest that spatial parameters of cell growth and tensions in the culture may affect the expression of junctions proteins. These parameters were analyzed using mathematical model of the 3D bioprinted cell culture. The finite element mechanical model includes an extracellular matrix and a group of regularly placed cells. The single-cell model comprises an idealized cytoskeleton, cortex, cytoplasm, and nucleus. The stress between cells is transferred via spring junctions. The model involves prestressed bar, tetrahedral, and shell elements. During the analysis, the transfer of stress generated by external pressure into the cytoskeleton is observed. Using the model, we have analyzed two different growth conditions, corresponding to a different elasticity of extracellular matrix. These results may contribute to a better understanding of the differences between various growth models.
